grammarChart.title: Passive Voice: Be + Past Participle
grammarChart.formation: The object of the active sentence becomes the subject of the passive sentence. The verb is changed to 'be' in the appropriate tense + the past participle of the main verb. The original subject can be omitted or included with 'by'.

active_to_passive_examples.passive: The book is read by the students.
The meal was cooked by the chef.

active_to_passive_examples.active: They will build a new bridge.
active_to_passive_examples.passive: A new bridge will be built by them.

active_to_passive_examples.active: The cat is chasing the mouse.
active_to_passive_examples.passive: The mouse is being chased by the cat.

explanation: The passive voice is used when the action is more important than the doer of the action, or when the doer is unknown or obvious.  In English, the passive voice is formed using a form of the verb 'to be' (am, is, are, was, were, been, being) followed by the past participle of the main verb. This structure shifts the focus from the agent (who performs the action) to the recipient of the action.
keyRules: Identify the object of the active sentence. This becomes the subject of the passive sentence.
Change the main verb to its past participle form (e.g., 'write' becomes 'written', 'eat' becomes 'eaten').
Add the appropriate form of the verb 'to be' before the past participle. The tense of 'be' must match the tense of the original active verb.
The original subject can be included using the preposition 'by' (e.g., 'by the teacher', 'by the company'). This is often omitted if the agent is unknown, unimportant, or generally understood.
Transitive verbs (verbs that take an object) can be made passive. Intransitive verbs (verbs that do not take an object) cannot.
azarNotes: In academic writing, especially for IELTS, the passive voice is frequently used to maintain objectivity and focus on the research or process rather than the researcher. Be mindful of overuse, as it can make your writing sound impersonal or vague if not used strategically.

examples.passive: Cars are produced by the company.
The mural was painted by the artist.

examples.active: They are building a new stadium.
examples.passive: A new stadium is being built.

examples.active: The students were discussing the topic.
examples.passive: The topic was being discussed by the students.

examples.active: The government has approved the new policy.
examples.passive: The new policy has been approved by the government.

examples.active: She had finished the report before the deadline.
examples.passive: The report had been finished before the deadline.

examples.active: We will launch the product next month.
examples.passive: The product will be launched next month.

examples.active: They are going to renovate the building.
examples.passive: The building is going to be renovated.

examples.active: They might have forgotten the key.
examples.passive: The key might have been forgotten.

commonMistakes: Using the wrong form of 'be' (e.g., 'The book is write' instead of 'The book is written').
Forgetting to use the past participle (e.g., 'The letter was send' instead of 'The letter was sent').
Incorrectly forming the passive with intransitive verbs (e.g., 'He arrived' cannot be 'He was arrived').
Confusing the active and passive structures in more complex sentences.
Omitting 'by' when the agent is important and needs to be specified in a context where it's not obvious.
ieltsTip: In IELTS Writing Task 2, use the passive voice to discuss processes, scientific findings, or general truths where the agent is less important. For example, 'It is believed that...', 'Research has shown that...', 'The results were analyzed...'.  In Task 1, describing processes (e.g., manufacturing, natural cycles) heavily relies on the passive voice.

quiz.question: Choose the correct passive form: The famous novel ______ by many people worldwide.
options: is read
was read
is reading
reads

quiz.question: Change the following active sentence to passive: The chef prepared a delicious meal.
options: A delicious meal prepared by the chef.
A delicious meal was prepared by the chef.
The chef was prepared by a delicious meal.
A delicious meal is prepared by the chef.
quiz.answer: A delicious meal was prepared by the chef.

quiz.question: Which sentence uses the passive voice correctly?
options: The letter will be sent tomorrow.
The letter will send tomorrow.
Tomorrow the letter will send.
They will be sending the letter tomorrow.
quiz.answer: The letter will be sent tomorrow.

quiz.question: Complete the sentence with the correct passive form: The ancient ruins ______ by archaeologists.
options: are discovered
were discovered
are discovering
discovered

quiz.question: Change the following active sentence to passive: The company has launched a new product.
options: A new product has launched by the company.
A new product is launched by the company.
A new product has been launched by the company.
The company has been launched by a new product.
quiz.answer: A new product has been launched by the company.
